text.tspan: Page 14, chapter 3 begins: graphs
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
DRAW IT
“Basically here we really need to make the
(visual) case of "why graphs" & why they are
so powerful & why they are everywhere”
Chapter 3 has one job: show, visually, why graphs, why
they are so powerful and why they are everywhere.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“it's not their fault, the industry
terminology is all over the place [left:
Reword, too harsh]”
In ordinary use a graph means any diagram, and the
industry's words are all over the place, so it is not the
reader's fault their definition differs from Dinis's: do
not make them feel guilty for it. Reword. (Dinis's answer,
19 October.)
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“give more analogies of what is a node & an
edge”
So, instead of correcting the reader, give more analogies
of what a node and an edge are: the words circled on the
page.
TOPICS FIRST, DETAILS UNDER THEM
“not relevant at this stage of the book”
The graphs book on graphs.sgit.ai is not for page 14.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“meaningless is too strong [and] each edge
is a signal”
'A node connected to nothing is literally meaningless'
overstates it; say instead that each edge is a signal.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“needs rewrite”
The three things people mean by graph needs rewriting.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“my use of graph → this is wrong ↓ a graph
node can be anything ↓ since a chart is a
graph too ↓ see the "thinking in graphs" or
"fractal semantic graphs"”
'My use of graph' points at the circled nodes and edges,
how Dinis uses the word; the arrow to 'never a chart,
never a figure' says that line is wrong, and too brutal.
In fractal semantic graphs anything can connect to
anything, so a node can be a chart or a figure, and a
chart is itself a graph, two-dimensional but still nodes
and edges. Point to thinking in graphs and fractal
semantic graphs: meaning comes from connectivity, and the
value is in what is on the other side of an edge. (Reading
confirmed by Dinis.)
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“[struck with a wave: In 2018 I left an
outline for a chapter called Graphs ...] see
Cut the 2018 outline.
ANSWERS TO FOR DINIS
“see graphs.sgit.ai”
The answer to For Dinis: the presentation on graphs is
graphs.sgit.ai.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“DEMEANING [circled: easier]”
That a Generation Z reader will find the chapter easier
than Dinis's generation did is demeaning.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“these kind of references are weird since
the reader has not read them [beside: In
Follow the rabbit holes]”
Do not cite a chapter the reader has not reached as if
they had read it.
